Ted was essentially correct about most of what he wrote, he missed or chose not to adress some major points, but he also overcorrected.
He pretty much nailed the power process thing. The vast majority of people are doing menial work that would make anyone go insane, I worked on a factory line for 2 years, I can't describe the anguish. You don't know what wage cucking is until you worked on one.

Then I worked construction for a year, and that was the best fucking job I ever had, manual labor. That's the moment I realized that man has a deep, biological need for simple, pragmatic, meaningful work. Simply put, manual labor, hunting, fishing and tilling the earth is fullfilling on an instictive level, which can't be compared to wage cucking. Work to live and live to work, instead of live to wage cuck for a month and get your little dopamine rush via paycheck so you can buy shit you don't need.

The industrial revolution changed the very nature of work, but technology on its own isn't bad, it's how we utilize it.
